title: WildSEEK: Evaluating Language Models for Information-Seeking
abstract: arXiv:2608.30683v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models are increasingly mediating information access to end users, urging a systematic evaluation of their responses for a fair and reliable information ecosystem. Existing evaluations, however, are often topic-specific or synthetic, limiting their ability to capture the complexity of "in the wild" information-seeking queries and the risks present in model responses. To address this gap, we introduce WildSEEK, a manually annotated dataset of 3k information-seeking queries from real user interactions, and an evaluation framework for LLM-generated responses. WildSEEK includes annotations for risk-sensitive domains (e.g. health and financial information), and distinguishes factoid queries from analytical queries which seek responses beyond facts. translated_title: WildSEEK：评估语言模型的信息检索能力
translated_abstract: 语言模型越来越多地充当终端用户获取信息的媒介，这迫切需要对模型回答进行系统性评估，以构建公平可靠的信息生态系统。然而，现有的评估方法往往局限于特定主题或采用合成数据，难以捕捉“真实场景中”信息检索查询的复杂性以及模型回答中存在的风险。为填补这一空白，我们提出了WildSEEK——一个包含3千条来自真实用户交互的信息检索查询的人工标注数据集，以及一个针对大语言模型生成回答的评估框架。WildSEEK包含对风险敏感领域（如健康和金融信息）的标注，并区分事实型查询与需要超越事实层面回答的分析型查询。我们在WildSEEK上训练分类器，分析了超过180万条真实用户查询。我们发现，超过三分之一的信息检索查询属于高风险，且更多为分析型查询。
tldr: 本文提出WildSEEK——基于3千条真实用户信息检索查询的人工标注数据集及大语言模型回答评估框架，通过分析超180万条真实查询，发现超过三分之一的信息检索查询属于高风险且多为分析型查询。
en_tdlr: WildSEEK introduces a manually annotated dataset of 3k real-world information-seeking queries and an evaluation framework for LLM responses, revealing through the analysis of 1.8M realistic user queries that over a third of information-seeking queries are high-risk and often analytical.
